svg.text: Three layers: what people use, the data it stands on, and the gateway and governance every request passes through
AI predictions · interactive dashboards · GenAI chat, RAG, forms and voice — what people use
capture → store → transform → serve; trains the models and indexes the documents
every request and every model call passes here — identity, tenancy, routing, policy, audit, monitoring
Five scenario kinds, one service instance per kind — tabular ML, RAG and GraphRAG, assisted forms, deep learning, and data products — each rendered by generic tabs plus an optional showpiece tab.
Interactive dashboards: the generic tabs, the showpiece tabs (maps, networks, globes), the data-product workspace and Superset. GenAI: the chat agents, all through the gateway below.
A scenario is a YAML file: it adds product content, never new UI or service code.

Row 1: the streaming data path of a data product (optional tiers: core, analytics, bi, governance). Row 2: batch jobs that train models and index documents, and the stores everything lives in — all scoped by org_id.
reads governed data, models and vectors — always scoped to the caller's tenant
every service checks identity and entitlement, and every LLM call goes through the gateway
Tenancy: the tenant is a Keycloak Organization; the entitlement check happens in the backend, never only in the UI. Governance supports a management system — it is not one.

Governance-ready by standards: declared AI-system metadata, a policy decision point, content-free CloudEvents, a hash-chained audit trail, decision records and an AI-BOM. Everything is off by default.
Dashed border = optional. See architecture-detailed.svg for every service-to-service call and architecture-data-platform.svg for the data path in detail.
